Duration: 20 Seconds
Style: High-End 3D Animated Family Film, Pixar-inspired Cinematic Quality, comedy with heart
Aspect Ratio: 9:16 vertical (framing must also work in 16:9)
Quality: 4K Ultra HD, 24 fps
Reference: Use the attached character sheet for Sam and Biscuit. Match faces, proportions, fur, outfit and room exactly.
Visual Style: Warm, natural morning light, soft shadows, gentle depth of field, expressive faces and fur detail. Palette: sage green, cream, honey wood, soft terracotta, golden sunlight. No neon, no fluorescent colors.

CHARACTERS (identical in every shot)
1. Sam: @ image1
2. Biscuit:  @ image 2 

OBJECT LEDGER
- Blanket (sage duvet): on Sam until Scene 4 → pulled off onto the floor on the right side of the bed (stays there) → Sam is uncovered, curled up for the rest of the video.
- Pillow: Scene 3 Sam pulls one over his head → Scene 4 he hugs it → it stays on the bed.
- Red leash: on the hook (Scene 2, clearly shown) → in Biscuit's mouth (Scene 7) → on Sam's face (Scene 7) → in his hand (Scene 9).
- Sock: mustard on Sam's left foot only, every shot.

SETUP → PAYOFF
- Leash on the hook (Scene 2) → Biscuit fetches it (Scene 7).
- Nose boop that wakes him (Scene 1) → Sam boops Biscuit's nose (Scene 10), which closes the loop.

PHYSICS RULES
- Biscuit weighs about 30 kg: the mattress compresses and Sam bounces when he jumps on. Nails click on the wooden floor, and paws slide on the wood when he pulls.
- Blanket tug-of-war follows real force: the blanket stretches taut, Sam's grip slips and Biscuit tumbles backward with the blanket over his head.
- Fur, ears, tail and the leash move with secondary motion and settle naturally. A happy wag moves his whole back half.
- Biscuit stays in the room. He cannot open doors.

PACING (THE EMOTION SETS THE SPEED)
Cozy and slow (0-4.5s) → escalating comedy, shots get shorter (4.5-13s) → the pivot, music thins and holds (13-15s) → warm and unhurried (15-20s).

SCENE 1 – THE BOOP (0–2.5s) HOOK
Extreme close-up. Biscuit's wet nose presses Sam's cheek on a pillow, boop, with huge brown eyes right above. Sam's eyebrow twitches. Warm sunlight on fur and stubble.
SFX: Soft room tone, a wet nose "boop", a happy sniff, gentle ukulele.

SCENE 2 – THE ROOM (2.5–4.5s)
Wide shot showing the whole room as mapped. Sam lies curled under the duvet, Biscuit stands beside the bed, tail sweeping. The red leash hangs on the hook by the door, clearly visible. Sam, face half in the pillow, mumbles.
SAM (sleepy mumble): "Five more minutes, Biscuit."
He rolls away from the dog toward the wall.

SCENE 3 – THE LICK (4.5–6s)
Biscuit puts his front paws on the mattress and licks Sam's ear. Sam winces and pulls the pillow over his head.
SFX: A lick, a muffled groan, mattress creak.

SCENE 4 – THE TUG (6–7.5s)
Biscuit grabs the blanket's corner in his teeth and pulls backward. The blanket stretches taut and Sam clings to the other end, then loses his grip. Biscuit tumbles backward with the blanket over his head. The blanket lands on the floor. Sam curls up into a ball, hugging the pillow.
SFX: Fabric tension, nails sliding on wood, a thump, a muffled "woof".

SCENE 5 – THE LANDING (7.5–9s)
Biscuit shakes the blanket off, takes a running jump onto the bed and bounces. Sam is thrown up an inch. Biscuit walks over him, circles once and plops on his chest.
SFX: Mattress spring, a human "oof", a happy huff.

SCENE 6 – THE STARE (9–10.5s)
Low angle. Biscuit lies on Sam's chest, nose to nose, staring without blinking. Sam cracks one eye open, sees the face an inch away, and deliberately shuts it again. Biscuit lets out a long sigh that blows Sam's hair.
SFX: A slow breath, a soft comedic string note.

SCENE 7 – THE LEASH (10.5–13s) PEAK
Biscuit hops down, trots to the door and, standing on his hind legs, pulls the leash off the low hook with his teeth. The leash swings and he trots back dragging it, jumps on the bed and drops the leash on Sam's face. It slides over his nose and the clip clinks on the bed frame. Sam opens one eye through the loop of the leash.
SFX: Nails clicking, leash rattle, a dull plop, a metallic clink, a held breath.

SCENE 8 – THE LOOK (13–15s) PIVOT
Music thins to a single warm note. Sam lifts the leash off his face. Biscuit sits beside him with his head tilted, tail sweeping slowly across the sheets, eyes full of hope, his left ear flipped inside out. Sam looks at him for a long beat.
SFX: Almost silent, a soft tail swish, one quiet guitar note.

SCENE 9 – THE YES (15–18s)
Sam breaks into a slow smile and sits up, the leash in his hand.
SAM (soft, warm): "Okay, okay. You win."
He ruffles Biscuit's ears. Biscuit's whole back half wags, and he licks Sam's chin. Sam laughs, swings his legs off the bed and puts both feet on the floor, mustard sock and all.
SFX: Rising warm ukulele, a laugh, a happy bark, a wagging tail thump.

SCENE 10 – THE LOOP (18–20s)
Extreme close-up mirroring Scene 1. Sam's finger boops Biscuit's nose. Biscuit sneezes, blinks and beams. Hold on the two faces in soft morning light, then a gentle fade.
SFX: A soft boop, a tiny sneeze, one final warm chime.

CAMERA RULES
- One main action per shot. Each shot begins from the previous shot's end state.
- Consistent screen direction: Biscuit goes toward the door on the left and returns to the bed on the right.
- Slow, smooth moves in Scenes 1-2 and 8-10, tight and fast cuts in Scenes 3-7.
- No random effects, no zoom gimmicks.

AUDIO
Playful acoustic score: ukulele, pizzicato strings, soft glockenspiel. Real foley for paws, nails, fabric and leash. Only two lines of dialogue, both sleepy and natural.

NEGATIVE: no neon colors, no extra characters, no extra pets, no extra furniture, no on-screen text, no logo or watermark, no scary or aggressive dog behavior, no changes to faces, outfit or fur, no distorted hands or paws, no objects not listed above, no realistic photo style.

IMPORTANT: Preserve the story, characters, setting, scene order and actions. Do not introduce additional characters or unrelated events.

[image1] is the exact reference for the main character: an adult Japanese woman in her mid-20s. [image2] is the rooftop location from every side. Never show any reference as a sheet, collage, or split-screen.

CHARACTER LOCK:
Keep her exactly as in [image1] throughout: same face, same dark brown short bob with see-through bangs, same white knee-length chiffon dress: the puff sleeves are sheer and airy, while the bodice and skirt have an opaque white lining, same white strap shoes. She holds a pale pink smartphone in her RIGHT hand, raised high above her face at arm's length, angled down at her for a classic high-angle selfie. PARTY GUESTS AND POSITIONS:
About ten adult guests in deep red, emerald, navy and gold evening clothes, all with different faces and hairstyles. They never look at the camera and never interact with her. Everyone, including her, stands on the rooftop floor on the same side of the railing. She stands in the open middle of the rooftop; the guests are around and behind her; the railing with bulbs and the skyline are at the far back. Nobody stands beyond the railing.
- Just to her left: a man and a woman at a small high table, clinking champagne glasses.
- Just behind her right shoulder: a waiter carrying a tray of glasses.

STYLE:
Photorealistic, dreamy night film. Warm bulb light, cool blue night sky, soft city bokeh. 9:16 vertical.
ONE CONTINUOUS SHOT WITH NO CUTS. The camera always stays level and upright; it never rolls or turns upside down. She stays in the frame the whole time.
No text, no signs, no logos, no subtitles anywhere.

LOCATION:
The rooftop in [image2] during a party: stone tiles, black railing with round warm bulbs, wooden planters, small high tables, the night skyline, and on the opposite side the small stairwell building with a plain door. A breeze blows a stream of soap bubbles and gold confetti past her and past the lens.

MOTION STRUCTURE (15s):

[0s-4.5s] SELFIE AT THE PARTY
First frame: medium-full shot from the front, she is already smiling with her hair moving in the breeze, bubbles streaming past, the party in full motion around her: the couple clinking glasses, the waiter walking past with his tray, guests dancing and laughing, a confetti cannon firing a gold burst. She looks around at the party, then lifts the phone high above her face in her right hand; the camera glides in to her face as she smiles up at the phone and says 「いくよ」.
Audio: light party pop music, chatter, breeze, her voice.

[4.5s] THE CLICK
She presses the shutter, smiling up at the phone with both eyes open (no wink yet). On the click, time stops completely: hair frozen mid-sway, every bubble and confetti piece frozen mid-flight, one small bubble just beside her left cheek, never in front of her face, frozen in the instant of bursting in a hanging spray of tiny droplets, the champagne frozen mid-splash between the couple's glasses, the waiter frozen mid-stride with a glass tipping off his tray, the dancers frozen mid-turn.
Audio: the click, then the music and every sound cut out at once.

[4.5s-8s] THE ORBIT
Nothing moves except the camera. It pulls back to medium-full distance and travels one full 360-degree circle around her, keeping her in the center of the frame, with a clear change of speed: it starts slowly while still in front of her so her frozen smile is clearly seen, accelerates hard as it swings around behind her, whipping past the frozen champagne splash, the waiter's tipping glass and the frozen guests, then slows down smoothly as it comes back around to her front.
Audio: near silence, only an airy camera whoosh that rises with the speed behind her and fades as it slows.

[8s-10.5s] ONLY ME
The camera glides in to a close-up of her face. Everything stays frozen. Only she moves: her eyes slide from the phone to the lens, she raises the index finger of her LEFT hand to her lips, "shh".
Audio: complete silence, then her soft "shh".

[10.5s-11s] THE WINK
Still in close-up, she gives one playful one-eyed wink: only her right eye closes while her left eye stays open, and on that wink the frozen bubble beside her cheek pops and time snaps back: bubbles and confetti fly on, the champagne splashes into the glasses, the waiter catches the glass, her hair sways.
Audio: the bubble pop on her wink, then the music and party sound drop back in on the beat.

[11s-15s] BACK TO THE START
The party is in full motion again. The camera glides back out to the same medium-full front framing as the very first frame. She giggles, glances around at the party as if nothing happened, and lifts the phone high again for another selfie, so the last frame matches the first frame for a seamless loop.
Audio: the music and party sound play on; her light giggle.

FROZEN-TIME RULE:
While time is frozen (4.5s-10.5s), nothing moves except the camera and, only from 8s to 10.5s, the woman in white. Every guest stays perfectly still: no blinking, no breathing, no drifting liquid. No new objects or people appear.

NOTES:
Start with strong motion on the very first frame so the freeze is obvious.
She is the only main character; the guests never become her double.
She is clearly an adult; the framing is respectful and never aims at her chest or under the dress.
Her outfit, hair and phone stay identical throughout. No bubble ever covers her face.
She says only 「いくよ」 and "shh". No text, no logos, no watermarks.

The entire sequence must feel like a continuous scene from a high-budget Korean action-comedy drama. Preserve the chronological order of every action described below.

CHARACTER AND ENVIRONMENT CONSISTENCY

Character 1 — The Blonde Schoolgirl

A young adult female student with long, straight blonde hair and bangs, wearing a dark navy Korean school uniform blazer, white shirt, striped ribbon tie, and pleated navy skirt. She sits at a classroom desk, calmly writing in her notebook. Her expression is initially indifferent and focused. Her face, hairstyle, outfit, and body proportions remain consistent throughout the video.

Character 2 — The Red-Haired Student

He behaves aggressively at first but becomes shocked and panicked when his own clothing catches fire. Maintain consistent facial features, hairstyle, outfit, and body proportions.

Character 3 — The Dark-Haired Schoolgirl

A young adult female student with long, dark hair, wearing a fitted navy school blazer, white shirt, striped tie, pleated navy skirt, and knee-high black socks. She appears later in the school hallway and confidently confronts the red-haired student.

ENVIRONMENT

A realistic Korean high-school classroom connected to a bright institutional hallway. The classroom contains wooden desks, student chairs, green chalkboards, classroom posters, large windows, and pale curtains. Natural daylight enters through the windows. The hallway has light-colored walls, classroom doors, and a polished floor.

Maintain consistent lighting, architecture, furniture placement, and spatial relationships between shots.

SHOT-BY-SHOT ACTION SEQUENCE

SHOT 1 — 0:00–0:02 | Calm Classroom Opening

Begin with a medium close-up of the blonde schoolgirl sitting at her desk, writing in an open notebook with a pen. Her head tilts slightly downward, and her long blonde hair falls naturally around her face.

The classroom remains active in the background, with students sitting at desks. Use a steady cinematic camera, shallow depth of field, soft daylight, and natural skin texture.

The girl remains focused on writing, seemingly unaware of the disturbance behind her.

SHOT 2 — 0:02–0:04 | The Burning Bag Is Thrown

Cut to a wider classroom composition.

The red-haired male student suddenly throws a black school bag that is already engulfed in bright orange flames toward the blonde girl.

The bag travels rapidly through the classroom with believable weight, momentum, and rotation. Flames flicker backward with the movement, producing realistic orange highlights and a small trail of smoke.

The blonde girl immediately reacts, turning toward the incoming bag and preparing to defend herself.

Keep the other students visible in the background, reacting with surprise.

SHOT 3 — 0:04–0:06 | The Blonde Girl's Counterattack

The blonde girl rises and performs a fast, controlled high side kick toward the incoming burning bag.

Her supporting foot remains planted firmly on the floor. Her hips rotate naturally, her kicking leg extends with convincing force, and her skirt, hair, blazer, and tie react to the sudden movement.

Her foot strikes the bag and redirects it back toward the red-haired student.

The camera briefly follows the movement of the bag, creating a dramatic sense of speed and impact.

The fire remains attached to the bag, with realistic flickering flames and motion blur.

Realistic handheld smartphone footage filmed by a crew member inside a helicopter hovering low over a steaming geothermal field in Iceland, vertical framing, shot from just behind and beside a second crewman at the open side door.

Subject: a crewman in a black flight helmet, olive-green flight suit and tan leather gloves works beside a huge open steel drum packed with thousands of dry wavy instant noodle blocks, a smaller drum of bright orange-red spice powder, and a bucket of chopped green onions and peas. Below: a wide round hot spring pool of bright turquoise water, rolling at a full boil, steam pouring off it, and right beside it a geyser vent in grey mineral crust, all surrounded by brown moss and black rock.

STAGE 1 — THE MIX (0-5s)
Close on the drum of dry noodle blocks. The crewman tips in the orange-red spice powder in a big cloud and the chopped green onions and peas, then stirs with a long metal paddle; the dry blocks rattle and clack.
End state: a drum of dry noodle blocks coated in orange spice with green bits through them.

STAGE 2 — THE POUR (5-10s)
He tilts the drum over the door sill and the dry noodle blocks pour out in a wide clattering stream; the camera tilts down and follows them into the boiling turquoise pool.
End state: the whole surface of the boiling pool is covered in floating noodle blocks.

STAGE 3 — THE COOK (10-15s)
Near top-down view. The blocks soften and loosen in the rolling boil, untangling into long wavy noodle strands that swirl around the pool; the spice spreads and the water turns a rich orange broth, steam billowing up.
End state: the pool is a giant swirling bowl of steaming orange noodle soup.

STAGE 4 — THE GEYSER (15-20s)
The geyser vent beside the pool rumbles, then erupts: a huge column of boiling water and steam blasts straight up, carrying masses of cooked noodles with it, rising toward the helicopter and growing bigger in frame every second.
End state: the steaming column of noodles reaches the open doorway.

STAGE 5 — THE SLURP (20-30s)
Hot cooked noodles splash down into a giant steel bowl wedged in the cabin, the bowl filling to the brim with orange broth and long noodles, steam rolling off it. The crewman grabs a fork the size of a garden rake, twirls up a huge tangle of noodles, slurps them in one long noisy slurp, broth splashing on his chin, and says "Two seconds, not two minutes." The second crewman lifts a long strand high with chopsticks and slurps it down.
End state: both crewmen hunched over the giant steaming bowl, eating, the geyser still steaming far below.

Camera: one continuous take, no cuts. Starts close on the drum, tilts down through the doorway to follow the pour, holds near top-down as the noodles cook, pulls back as the geyser column rises, then swings into the cabin and ends close on the giant bowl and the slurp. Light rotor vibration shake throughout, a jolt when the geyser erupts. The door sill with grey diamond-quilted padding and a metal rail stays in the bottom of frame while looking down.

Light and look: soft overcast northern daylight, bright turquoise hot spring water, grey mineral crust, brown moss and black rock, thick white steam, rich orange broth and glossy yellow noodles with green onions, real phone-camera detail and slight compression, true scale, photorealistic.

Audio: constant helicopter rotor thump and wind buffeting, dry noodle blocks rattling and clacking, spice powder shaking, a long clattering hiss as the blocks pour out, the deep rolling bubble of the boiling pool, a low underground rumble and a roaring whoosh as the geyser erupts, broth splashing into the steel bowl, loud slurping, then the one short line and laughter. No music.

Continuity: one drum, one hot spring, one geyser, two crewmen whose helmets, flight suits and gloves stay the same; the noodles stay long, glossy and yellow, never burnt or mushy; no brand names, packaging or logos anywhere; the boiling water stays below the helicopter except the noodles that land in the bowl; nobody is scalded or hurt.

Flash に入れたプロンプト全文と、参照画像3枚です。参照画像は2本とも同じ。

12秒 / 720p / 16:9 / 音あり

2.5 版との違いは、Stage 1〜3 の末尾にある「End state: …」の3文だけです。

[Generation Goal]
Create one continuous FPV-style take of Jin sizing up a low-rise commercial building in the early night just after sunset, free-climbing its exterior service route with fast but heavy, physical parkour, sprinting across the rooftop without stopping, and leaping across a road roughly seven meters wide to the rooftop of the facing building, where he lands, rolls, and comes up into a low ready crouch.

[Reference Material Roles]
@Image 1 defines only the look of the district: corrugated-metal and concrete surfaces, exposed pipes, bundled cables, warm amber practical lights, wet reflective surfaces and hazy neon towers in the far distance. Do not use its street layout, its people or its camera composition.
@Image 2 defines the shapes and rooftop character of Neo-East buildings: blocky low-rise structures with flat roofs, parapets, rooftop water tanks, air-conditioning units, antennas, external steel staircases, awnings and laundry lines, with harbor haze beyond. Do not use its aerial viewpoint or its camera composition.
Jin corresponds to @Image 3. Use only this one man's face, brown ribbed knit cap over untidy black hair, stubble, weathered dark-brown knee-length coat over a charcoal henley shirt, dark trousers and worn leather boots. Do not use the studio background or the multi-view sheet layout.

[Physical Set]
It is early night, just after sunset: the sky still holds a deep blue with the last amber afterglow low above the rooflines, and the street practicals are already lit. The building Jin climbs is a three-story multi-tenant commercial building of the kind defined by @Image 2: small businesses stacked one per floor, mismatched tenant signboards on the facade, a flat roof with a parapet. Its exterior wall carries a climbable service route from bottom to top, roughly one solid hold per floor: a concrete ledge, a reinforced air-conditioner cage, a thick metal pipe running horizontally across the facade, then the parapet of the flat roof. A TV antenna on a metal mast stands on the rooftop. A road runs between this building and the facing building: the facing building stands about seven meters away across the road, and its flat rooftop sits about one meter lower. Warm amber street lights burn on the road below the gap.

[Event Script]
Opening state - sizing up: A low-angle 24mm wide shot from behind Jin's right shoulder, about four meters away. Jin stands at the base of the wall and looks up. Following his gaze, the camera tilts up the facade and introduces the three-story building's shape and the route in order: the stacked tenant signboards, the concrete ledge, the caged air conditioner, the horizontal pipe, the parapet, and the TV antenna silhouetted at the roofline against the fading afterglow sky. The camera tilts back down to Jin as he lowers his chin.
Stage 1 - Climb: Jin takes two accelerating steps and attacks the wall in a powerful parkour climb of three contacts, each one loaded with his full body weight: his right boot drives off the concrete ledge, his left boot slams onto the reinforced air-conditioner cage and the cage rattles under the load, his right boot hits the horizontal pipe and the pipe flexes with a dull metallic ring. At every contact his knees compress and load for a beat before the next explosive push upward, and his weathered coat swings and settles with the momentum. He drives one final push off the wall, catches the parapet with both hands, boots scraping the wall as his arms haul his full weight over, and vaults onto the roof, landing in a deep knee bend with one palm briefly touching the concrete. The climb stays fast and fluid, but gravity visibly loads every hold and he wins each rise with muscle. Nothing floats. The camera rises close behind his right side, shuddering slightly at each impact, and as he vaults, his back briefly fills the frame. End state: Jin is on the roof in a deep knee bend, one palm on the concrete.
Stage 2 - Rooftop sprint: Jin rises out of the landing directly into a sprint, three accelerating strides across the flat rooftop toward the gap-side parapet, his coat streaming behind him, his boots hammering the concrete. End state: Jin reaches the gap-side parapet at full speed.
Stage 3 - The leap: Without breaking stride he plants his right boot on top of the parapet and drives off it in one explosive leap out over the road. For one beat he is fully airborne: body stretched forward, arms swinging through, coat snapping in the wind, the amber street lights sliding past on the road far below him. Then gravity reclaims him and he drops toward the facing rooftop, which sits about one meter lower. End state: Jin is just above the facing rooftop, about to touch down.
Ending state: Jin lands hard on the facing rooftop in a deep knee bend, folds his momentum into a forward roll over his right shoulder, and comes up out of the roll into a low ready crouch, still facing his direction of travel. The camera crosses the gap with him at his right shoulder, shudders once on his landing, then settles level behind his right shoulder and holds the final composition steady: Jin crouched low on the new rooftop among its water tanks and air-conditioning units, the crossed gap and the first building behind him, and hazy neon-edged towers beyond under the last of the afterglow. He holds this crouch as the take ends.

[Visual and Camera Treatment]
Photorealistic live action in the early night just after sunset: deep-blue sky with a fading amber afterglow low above the rooflines, warm amber practical lights already lit in the streets below. 24mm wide-angle lens, one continuous FPV-style follow: a slow tilt up and back down the facade for the sizing-up, low angle dominant during the climb, then a fast follow at Jin's right shoulder through the sprint and the leap, crossing the gap with him, resolving to level as he comes up from the roll. The camera shudders slightly at each climbing impact and once at the final landing. Deep focus keeps the climbing route, the rooftop, the gap and the facing building readable. Wet metal and concrete reflections, humid haze, fine film grain and tactile real-world textures.

[Audio]
Jin keeps his mouth naturally closed. No dialogue, narration, background music, subtitles or on-screen text. <A slow breath as he looks up.> <Each boot impact lands heavy on concrete and metal: the cage rattles, the pipe rings dully.> <Both hands slap the parapet, and a hard effort breath as he hauls himself over.> <Sprinting footfalls hammer the rooftop concrete.> <Wind rushes past during the airborne beat.> <A heavy landing thud, then fabric scuffing concrete through the roll.>

[Maintain Consistency]
Jin remains one continuous person through the whole take; keep his identity, face, knit cap, clothing, body structure and limb count stable through the look-up, the climb, the sprint, the leap and the landing. The order of the climbing contacts does not change, and the camera stays behind his right side throughout. His travel direction never reverses. There is exactly one leap across the gap, and he crosses it exactly once: the take ends with him crouched on the facing rooftop, and he does not return.

Characters and setting:
Pelican — a stylized cartoon big white pelican, eighty centimeters tall when standing, round and plump, white feathers all over with black wingtips; a thick, long neck; a small tuft of messy feathers sticking back on top of its head; round yellow eyes with black pupils, a ring of pink skin around each eye; a very long beak, the upper beak flat and grey-pink with a small hook at the tip, and an orange-yellow throat pouch hanging under the lower beak — the pouch is a thin, stretchy layer of skin; short orange legs and very large webbed feet. It is the same pelican throughout the film, with its pouch in three states:
  Pouch normal — the pouch is tucked up against the underside of the lower beak. This is the state in Shots 1 to 3.
  Pouch stretched into a ball — the pouch is stretched by the pufferfish inside into a perfectly round ball bigger than the pelican's head, hanging in front of its chest, the skin thin, tight, translucent and shiny, with a dozen or so small points poking out from inside across the surface; the beak is forced open and cannot close; what is inside cannot be seen, only the points poking out. This is the state from Shot 4 until it coughs out the pufferfish in Shot 8. The ball is the pouch skin itself stretched out, attached to the lower beak — it is not an object held in the mouth.
  Pouch stretched out and saggy — the pouch has been stretched loose into a big slack, wrinkled sheet of orange-yellow skin, deflated and full of folds, hanging from the lower beak down past the chest; all its feathers are wet, clumped in strands and beaded with water. This is the state from after it coughs out the pufferfish in Shot 8 through Shot 12; the pouch never goes back to normal.
Pufferfish — a stylized cartoon little pufferfish, the same one throughout the film, in two states:
  Normal — only the size of a ping-pong ball, short and round; pale sandy-yellow back with small dark-brown round spots, creamy white belly; smooth skin with no raised spines; two very large round eyes, a little dopey; a tiny pouting mouth showing two little buck teeth; small translucent fins.
  Puffed into a ball — its body is inflated into a perfectly round ball four or five times its normal size, covered all over with short sharp spines; color, spots, eyes, mouth and fins are the same as normal, and the eyes, mouth and fins stay their original size, looking tiny on the big round ball.
Dock (one location, seen from two directions) — a seaside in the early morning. An old wooden piling covered in barnacles stands in clear shallow seawater, two or three steps away from a wooden dock; the top of the piling is flat and stands more than a meter above the water; the piling has weathered wood grain, and the section around the waterline and below is covered in grey-white barnacles and a little green seaweed; the water is very clear, a pale blue-green, with the sand and stones on the bottom visible.
  Facing the sea — behind the piling is open sea all the way to the horizon; ove the horizon, low, with a golden streak of reflection on the water; the skygoes from orange-pink at the horizon to pale blue above, with a few wisps of thin cloud; in the distance, one or two tiny fishing-boat silhouettes and an orange buoy. Shots 1, 2, 3,
7, 8, 9, 10 and 12 use this side.
  Facing the dock — behind the piling is the side of the wooden dock: a row of thick wooden posts at uneven heights holding up an old plank walkway, with shrimp traps, mooring rope
and an old wooden crate on it, and old tires hanging along its edge; farther 's huts on shore; the sun is not visible, and warm golden sunlight comes frombehind the camera. Shots 4, 5 and 11 use this side.

⚠️ Characters: there is only one pelican and one pufferfish in the whole film. Pouch normal, stretched into a ball, and saggy are three states of the same pelican; normal and puffed
are two states of the same pufferfish; two pelicans or two pufferfish never a
⚠️ Scale: the pufferfish is normally only the size of a ping-pong ball — a single one of the pelican's webbed feet is bigger than it; when puffed up it is a ball slightly bigger

waterline of the piling. After the pelican tumbles off the top, it lies on thiling. When both are in frame on the water, the pelican is on screen left andthe pufferfish on screen right.
⚠️ This video has strictly 12 shots, all joined by hard cuts. Do not add extrfects.
⚠️ No dialogue, no narration, no subtitles, no background music in the whole film; only animal sounds and on-location sound effects.

[Shot 1] (0–2s)
Camera: 24mm, camera right at the water surface, tilted slightly up, locked o
Background: facing the sea — the piling is at screen left, extending up out of frame; behind it, the sea and the early-morning sky.
Action:
- ① First frame: the little pufferfish (normal state) is in the near foreground, lower center-left of frame, about one fifth of frame height, its body just under the clear water surface, right up against the piling at screen left, nibbling the barnacles otle buck teeth; a big shadow has already fallen over it, and the pelican's open grey-pink beak is already at the top of frame, stabbing down toward it. The pelican's body is on top of the piling above the frame; only the plunging beak and a length of neck are

- ② The beak plunges into the water, scoops up the little pufferfish along with a pouchful of water, and pulls up out of frame; a spray of water droplets of different sizes fills

Sound: waves and distant seagulls as a bed; a "splash".

[Shot 2] (2–4s) (hard cut)
Camera: 35mm, camera level with the top of the piling, shot from its front ri

Action:

26.0–28.0秒：日落时分，林澈在海岸线上空约150米处朝镜头方向步行，脚下没有任何东西。双腿交替迈步，双臂自然前后摆动，肩膀放松，头向左右转动看下方的海岸和城市，披风自然垂落并轻微摆动。

NEGATIVE / 全片负面约束：
慢动作、子弹时间、定格；换装；第二个主角；眼睛发光；手掌放出能量光；可读的文字、线路屏字样、车牌号、船名、Logo、水印、字幕；威亚绳、绿幕、支架；人物凭空出现或凭空消失；公交车翻车、快艇翻覆、多人落水、爆炸；吊装带缠绕在人身上；钢梁弯曲变形；出水后衣服和披风是干的；肢体穿插、多出手指；身体比例变形；塑料CG质感；镜头剧烈乱晃；角色脸部漂移；发型变化；服装变化；披风消失；战衣变成其他款式；靴子变化；角色突然变成其他女性。

Create a 30-second ultra-realistic 16:9 1080p live-action video filmed like casual handheld footage by a friend using an older digital camera.

A young French woman in her early 20s, with long naturally loose dark-brown hair, wears a dark green knit sweater, black wide-leg trousers, white sneakers, and carries a small burgundy handbag. Keep her face, identity, hairstyle, outfit, proportions, and handbag identical throughout.

LOCATION: A small independent movie theater in Lyon, France, around 8:30 PM. The theater is almost completely empty. Red fabric seats, dark carpet, narrow aisles, dim wall lights, small ticket counter, fictional movie posters, projector-room window, and a quiet lobby. Use only fictional movie titles and posters.

CAMERA: Raw handheld consumer-camera footage. Slight natural shake, imperfect framing, autofocus hunting, exposure adjustment, mild digital noise, natural motion blur and compression. No stabilization, cinematic bokeh, professional lighting, smooth tracking, or commercial/trailer aesthetic.

0-5s , EMPTY LOBBY  
Camera follows her through the nearly empty lobby. She looks around and quietly says, “We're really early.” She smiles and enters the screening room.

5-10s , FINDING A SEAT  
She walks down the aisle and chooses a middle seat. She sits naturally, compressing the fabric seat, and places her burgundy handbag beside her.

10-15s , PROJECTOR  
She looks toward the screen. A realistic projector beam cuts through the darkness, with dust visible only inside the beam. She looks at the camera and whispers, “Look at that.” Camera tilts slightly toward the projector.

15-20s , POPCORN  
She notices a half-empty popcorn bucket on a nearby empty seat. She picks it up, looks confused, and says, “Someone forgot this.” She places it on the floor beside the seat.

20-25s , LIGHTS DIM  
The theater lights suddenly become darker. The projector becomes brighter and softly illuminates her face. She looks around briefly, then settles into her seat.

25-30s , QUIET MOMENT  
Camera stays behind her shoulder as she watches the screen. Only soft fictional screen light illuminates her face. She briefly turns and smiles at the camera. Autofocus becomes slightly soft as the camera moves, then the video ends naturally.

AUDIO: Natural theater ambience only,quiet footsteps, carpet movement, seat sounds, fabric movement, distant lobby sounds, projector fan, electrical hum, room echo, and quiet whispers. NO background music. Movie audio must be indistinct and completely original.

REALISM: Physically accurate projector light, dust, shadows, seat compression, handbag deformation, hair and clothing movement, and screen illumination. No recognizable movie footage or dialogue.

NEGATIVE PROMPT: CGI, animation, 3D render, plastic skin, beauty filter, face morphing, identity drift, extra fingers, malformed hands, duplicated people, floating objects, impossible lighting, fake projector beam, excessive HDR, oversaturation, artificial bokeh, cinematic trailer look, perfect stabilization, exaggerated acting, horror effects, wardrobe changes, hairstyle changes, continuity errors, subtitles, captions, logos, watermarks, real movie posters, copyrighted footage, copyrighted dialogue, copyrighted music.

FINAL STYLE: Quiet, ordinary, slightly nostalgic, intimate, imperfect, and genuinely believable,like a friend casually recording an almost-empty cinema before a movie starts.

30 seconds, 16:9, cinematic animation with realistic adult human proportions and real materials, normal-speed motion, natural motion blur. One continuous nighttime campfire dinner scene told in 8 cuts. Three adult women talk about life after leaving the dead city. A small detection drone performs routine patrol and shoots down one harassing crow. The guard incident must not interrupt the conversation rhythm: at most a casual glance, no panic, no standing in alarm, no sword-grabbing, no stopping the fish roast. Outside the fence is harsh and dangerous; by the fire, they can still read each other’s eyes and smiles. All intelligible dialogue must use only the English lines listed below. No subtitles, narration, opening or ending cards.

[Reference Responsibilities]
Image 1 = Alin, wounded platinum-haired adult woman. Lock face shape, light eyes, blunt bangs, torn white top, blue jeans, boots, and scar positions. Add one weathered gray-brown blanket over her legs without changing the clothing. She remains weak from severe injury and stays seated and supported throughout.
Image 2 = Lisa, short blonde adult woman. Lock face shape, blue eyes, orange-brown leather jacket with pale fur collar, inner layers, dark skirt, waist bag, and ankle boots. Never rename her Elin.
Image 3 = Hia, dark-haired adult woman with a bun. Lock East Asian face, hair ornament, dark blue-black and deep red embroidered long coat, belt, and boots. Her sheathed long sword stays on the outer side of her bench for the whole scene; never rename her Jia.
Image 4 = the only environment reference. Keep the spatial relationship among shipping container, canopy, corrugated fence, gate, fire pit, benches, water jar, and worktable; convert daytime to deep night. Use the main wide view to set layout; the fire-pit detail view only informs materials and structure. Render as one complete location. Do not include reference layouts, labels, numbers, split panels, or character turnarounds.
Image 5 = the only detection drone: orange-yellow spherical shell, central observation eye, two side-deploying firing units. Keep the reference structure. It shoots short pulse lasers; the center eye observes, the laser emits from the side barrels.
Image 6 = bloodthirsty crow reference for feathers, beak, claws, and dark red eyes. Keep normal real crow size and avian skeletal structure. Eyes only catch dim reflections and do not glow outward.

Only three humans appear: Alin, Lisa, Hia, plus one drone. Character identity, costume, prop design, and material finish come only from their own references and cannot be swapped.

[Real Scale]
All three women follow normal adult female scale, roughly 1.65–1.75 m standing height. Perspective may change screen size but not world scale.
Crows are normal-sized: about 40–45 cm beak to tail, 80–90 cm wingspan, never giant ravens or raptors.
The drone is small: folded sphere about 12 cm diameter, about 20 cm wide when firing units are deployed, small enough to hold in one hand, smaller than an adult head and clearly smaller than a same-depth crow torso. It hovers about 2.2–2.6 m above ground. Never stage it as a large UAV or manned craft. Keep fence posts, canopy edges, or crows in frame as scale references, and avoid ultra-close wide-angle enlargement.
There are only three fish, each about 25 cm long, skewered on thin branches about 60 cm long, with visible tail fins and blistered skin.
The stone-ring fire pit is about 1.2 m wide. The burning zone stays modest: mostly glowing coals with flames about 20–35 cm high. Fish roast over the coal edge nearest the characters, not in the center of the flames.

[Locked Space and Blocking]
Use the main viewing direction from the gate side toward the rear container as the scene axis, called south-to-north for this scene only. Fire pit center is the origin. Screen right is east; the container side is north.

A = Alin = Image 1. Fixed north of the fire, slightly west, around (-0.35, 1.65)m. She leans against a wooden crate with an old cushion, body turned south-southeast so she can see the other two. Her head and shoulders must always remain visible between them and never be fully blocked by furniture or bodies.
B = Lisa = Image 2. Starts seated on the north end of the northwest bench, around (-0.95, 0.45)m, body facing southeast, able to turn toward Hia. She is about 1.3 m from Alin, feet planted on clear ground outside the fire ring.
C = Hia = Image 3. Fixed on the northeast bench, around (0.95, 0.45)m, body facing southwest toward Lisa. Both feet stay grounded. She never changes seats or stands.

Before 18 seconds, all three stay fixed at their ground positions. From 18–21 seconds, Lisa takes the largest fish, rises from the north end of her bench, walks two small steps along the west side of the fire to crouch beside Alin at about (-0.90, 1.55)m, with shoulders roughly 0.55 m apart. She always avoids the stone ring and Hia, never crosses the fire, never passes through furniture, never teleports. After 21 seconds she stays there until the end.

Look: photoreal live-action blockbuster VFX, two giant mechanical warriors in a real Times Square, New York, bright midday sun, blue sky, crisp hard shadows, neutral daylight grade, heavy motion blur on fast moves, 35mm anamorphic lens feel. Camera feel: aggressive chase-cam that tracks the fighters through the air, short heavy camera jolts on every impact, then a slow-motion close-up for the kill and a top-down drone view for the aftermath. Pacing: relentless, 10 fast shots, almost all of the fight airborne several stories above the street; the only slow moment is the final cut. No sparks, no glowing particles, no blood, no on-screen text, no readable logos on the billboards.

CHARACTERS:
- A, THE MECH SAMURAI (hero): a hulking humanoid armored machine, about 2.5 m tall. Gunmetal-black armor plates with deep violet panels and acid yellow-green plates printed with black round dots; a horned black helmet with two short swept-back horns; a bulky mechanical backpack with black hoses and pistons; a ragged black cloth half-cape hanging from the back; heavy armored boots; wields TWO long silver katanas, one in each hand. Signature in every shot: the violet and dotted yellow-green armor and the two katanas.
- B, THE MECHANICAL REAPER (villain): a taller (about 3.5 m), gaunt mechanical reaper. Face: an ivory-white ceramic deer-skull mask with a red painted crosshair circle on the forehead, red painted streaks down the cheeks and two glowing red eyes; huge branching ivory antlers with red tips; long tattered white-and-crimson cloth robes and streamers that whip in the wind; underneath, a bronze and gunmetal chassis of gears, cables, round red lens-like discs on the chest and hanging chains with brass medallions; carries an enormous scythe with a dark crimson curved blade and a small red lantern-vessel hanging from it. B can dissolve into a cloud of dense BLACK MIST and reassemble elsewhere. Signature in every shot: the white deer-skull mask with antlers and the red-white tattered robes.

LOCATION: Times Square, Manhattan, midday: giant LED billboards (one huge screen glowing blue and white), tall stone and brick office buildings with rows of windows, green construction fences and wooden scaffolding on rooftops, a long straight avenue running into the distance with yellow taxis, crosswalks and tiny pedestrians far below. Damage stays and accumulates: shattered windows, dust, a crater in the street.

SHOT 1 (00:00.0-00:02.0) — Thrown into the air. Starts already mid-action. Camera low at street level beside the asphalt: A skids backward toward camera under a sidewalk scaffold shed, boots tearing a trench in the asphalt; at 00:00.5 A slams into a building column in a burst of pale gray dust and concrete chunks (camera jolts); at 00:01.0 A rebounds off the wall beside a giant billboard and launches upward; the camera swings up behind A's right shoulder as A flies high over the avenue at 00:01.5, the whole of Times Square and the long avenue visible far below. MUST SHOW: a dense cloud of black mist condensing in the air ahead of A on the right side of frame.
SHOT 2 (00:02.0-00:04.0) — Missed strike. Wide lateral tracking shot: A (left) and B (right) meet in midair high above an intersection, B's robes streaming; A slashes, B dissolves and A passes through empty air past a rooftop with a green construction fence (00:02.5). Sharp upward pan at 00:03.0: low angle on A silhouetted against a gigantic blue-and-white LED billboard, katanas spread, B a red-white shape diving from the top-left corner; at 00:03.5 the impact throws A into a dark LED panel framework that buckles into rigid black rectangles.
SHOT 3 (00:04.0-00:05.4) — Clash on the facade. Side tracking shot along a tan stone building facade, the busy street far below on the left: B lunges in from the right swinging the scythe, A blocks with both katanas (00:04.5, B's deer-skull mask and antlers clearly visible right next to A); B's blow launches A horizontally across the frame into the windows (00:05.0, strong motion blur).
SHOT 4 (00:05.4-00:06.3) — Inside the office. Interior of an empty dim office floor: the window bursts and the room fills with a rolling gray dust cloud under a flickering ceiling fluorescent tube; A lands in a low sliding crouch on the floor, both katanas held out, bright windows behind.
SHOT 5 (00:06.3-00:07.3) — Bursting out. Exterior wide: A explodes out of the stone facade in a cloud of debris and leaps into open air, modern glass skyscrapers of Midtown in the background, blue sky; MUST SHOW: B re-forming from a swirl of black mist in the air at lower right, then dashing up toward A.
SHOT 6 (00:07.3-00:08.8) — Midair duel. Medium tracking shot between the buildings: A and B collide in midair, A's katana against B's scythe shaft; the crimson scythe blade sweeps over A's head with its little red lantern swinging; A is kicked and spins head-over-heels (00:08.0), then is flung backward toward the buildings in heavy motion blur (00:08.5).
SHOT 7 (00:08.8-00:10.0) — Through the scaffolding. High angle: A crashes through rooftop wooden scaffolding at the corner of a tall stone building in a burst of splintered planks and dust; at 00:09.5 the camera looks steeply down past A: B dives from the top of frame toward A, the street with red and blue billboards far below.
SHOT 8 (00:10.0-00:11.9) — The dive. Top-down drone view looking straight down at the street: A drops from a rooftop ledge, katanas out, falling toward a fresh round crater blasted in the asphalt, pale dust ring around it; B's small figure vanishes into black mist on the street; A free-falls past the camera toward the crater, tiny pedestrians and red storefronts at the edges.
SHOT 9 (00:11.9-00:13.9) — The final cut, slow motion. Extreme close-up: one katana slices horizontally across B's chest in a blur (00:12.0); then a locked-off close-up on B's ivory deer-skull mask, the silver katana blade held flat across the bottom of the frame, B's red eyes glowing (00:12.5) and then going dark (00:13.0); at 00:13.5 the mask splits down the middle, revealing gunmetal gears, pistons and cables inside. MUST SHOW: the red crosshair circle on the white skull forehead, centered in frame.
SHOT 10 (00:13.9-00:15.3) — Breakdown. Top-down view straight down on the cratered street: B's body bursts apart outward into hundreds of solid pieces: gears, brass medallions, white ceramic antler fragments, red cloth shreds, chains; at 00:14.5 the camera rises slightly as the debris lies scattered across the cracked asphalt and pale gray dust slowly settles.

SOUND: no dialogue. Hybrid cinematic percussion score with deep booms on every hit (no song). Asphalt ripping and concrete crash (shot 1), sword whoosh and a hollow mist whoosh when B vanishes, LED panels cracking (shot 2), heavy metal-on-metal clang (shot 3), glass shatter and muffled dust roar inside (shot 4), debris explosion (shot 5), rapid clangs and a kick thud (shot 6), splintering wood (shot 7), rushing wind on the dive (shot 8), near-silence in the slow motion with one sharp ringing blade slice and a ceramic crack (shot 9), a final crunching metal burst and clattering parts (shot 10).

Create a complete 15-second Halloween creature-party comedy in horizontal 16：9, accompanied by an original Halloween pop song with English vocals.

Prioritise adorable characters, playful tussling, expressive reactions, and a clear comedic twist. Cosmetics are story props only. No product beauty shots, logo close-ups, or advertising-style ending.

VISUAL STYLE
Polished 3D animation with soft, fluffy fur, rounded little paws, and expressive eyes. A warm cream and pumpkin-orange palette with lilac accents. Soft, bright lighting. Cute, lively, and mischievous—never dark or frightening.

SETTING
A Halloween dressing room just before a party: a low vanity, a round mirror, glowing pumpkin lanterns, paper bats, and colourful fairy lights. On the vanity are a powder puff, an eyeshadow palette, makeup brushes, and one uncapped berry-red lipstick. Keep the props sparse enough to leave room for clear character movement.

THREE CONSISTENT CHARACTERS
• An orange kitten wearing a crooked miniature witch hat. Impatient and expressive; its pupils widen and its tail rises when it spots something exciting.
• A cream-coloured puppy wearing a short purple vampire cape. Loves admiring itself. A slightly crooked star is already painted on one cheek.
• A white bunny wearing a pumpkin headband. Looks innocent but is the cleverest of the three. Its long ears move expressively.

Keep their appearances, costumes, and relative sizes consistent. Their stylised paws can naturally grasp objects but must never become human hands.

TIMELINE — EXACTLY 15 SECONDS

0–3s | THE DISCOVERY
Start immediately with all three creatures squeezed together in front of the mirror, busily applying Halloween makeup.
The puppy pats its nose with a powder puff and gives a tiny sneeze. The kitten’s witch hat slips down, and it quickly pushes it back into place.

The bunny picks up the only berry-red lipstick. The kitten and puppy notice it simultaneously, their eyes lighting up.

They exchange an unmistakable “Me first!” look and reach towards it on a strong musical beat. Enter the conflict quickly. No establishing shot.

3–7s | THE TUSSLE

The kitten gets hold of the lipstick first. The puppy gently grips the kitten’s lipstick-holding wrist and pulls it closer. The kitten wraps its other paw around its own wrist and pulls back.
Make the contact relationships unmistakable: the kitten holds the same lipstick throughout; the puppy pulls the kitten’s wrist, never the exposed lipstick tip.
They tug left once, then right once, in time with the beat. Their bodies lean comically, their little feet shuffle on the rug, and their ears and cape bounce with the movement.

The kitten puffs out its cheeks. The puppy wrinkles its nose. Both remain focused on the lipstick. The struggle feels like baby animals competing over a toy—gentle and funny, never aggressive.

The bunny watches from side to side, raises a paw as if trying to intervene, then realises neither is paying attention.

7–11s | THE COMEDIC TWIST

The tugging briefly reaches a stalemate, with the lipstick held steady between them.

The bunny gets an idea. It quietly leans in and lightly brushes the puppy’s nose with the spare powder puff.
The puppy gives a short sneeze and releases the kitten’s wrist. Still pulling backwards, the kitten accidentally draws one bold berry-red streak across its own cheek with the lipstick. The lipstick touches only the cheek, well away from the eyes.
The music briefly stops. All three freeze.

The kitten looks in the mirror, touches its cheek, then suddenly lifts its chin and proudly poses like a supermodel, treating the accidental streak as its own brilliant Halloween makeup invention.

The puppy and bunny go from surprise to uncontrollable giggles, their ears twitching and shoulders bouncing.

Clearly show the sequence: accident, reaction, then confidently turning the mistake into a look.

11–15s | THE PARTY FINISH

The chorus returns. The kitten proudly strikes a playful claw pose. The puppy and bunny squeeze in on either side.

———

Together, they perform two simple synchronised movements: sway from side to side, then raise their paws in a cute “Boo!” pose.

Their rivalry has turned into shared fun. The kitten still has the red cheek streak, the puppy still has powder on its nose, and the laughing bunny has one ear higher than the other.

Hold their final silly group-photo pose for the last half-second, with warm pumpkin lights glowing behind them.

End on their faces, personalities, and friendship. Cosmetics remain incidental props on the vanity. No isolated product shot.

ORIGINAL MUSIC — SPECIFIC DIRECTION
Compose an original 15-second English-language Halloween bubblegum-pop song at approximately 120 BPM in 4/4 time. Sweet, playful, catchy, and bouncy.

Use:
• A soft but clearly defined kick drum.
• Crisp handclaps and a light shaker.
• Short, springy bass notes.
• A recurring four-note melodic hook played by xylophone and a plucked synth.
• Small touches of toy piano and mysterious glockenspiel.

Use playful minor-key colour to suggest Halloween while keeping the overall mood bright and adorable. No heavy bass, horror screams, or epic orchestral scoring.

Use a clear, cheerful, playful pop singing voice with a smiling delivery. Add gentle layered backing vocals to “Boo!” Keep the melody original; do not quote an existing song.

Use these four short lyric lines. Leave space for character reactions and comedy. Do not rush the singing:

“Boo! Boo! Who are you?”
“A little monster, cute like you!”
“Oops! That’s my spooky look!”
“Boo! Boo! Look at you!”

MUSIC AND ACTION TIMING
0–3s: Sing the first line during the makeup activity and discovery of the lipstick.
3–7s: Sing the second line during the tussle. Synchronise the left and right pulls with distinct drum beats.
7–9s: Pause the singing, leaving only light plucked accompaniment. After the sneeze, punctuate the accidental cheek streak with one short xylophone note, followed by approximately half a second of comedic silence.
9–12s: Sing the third line as the kitten confidently reveals its accidental makeup look.
12–15s: Sing the final line over the group dance. Finish with coordinated handclaps and a short, playful musical ending. Do not cut the music off abruptly.

CHARACTER VOCALISATIONS AND FOLEY
The creatures never speak intelligible words and never lip-sync to the background song.

Give each an original, distinct vocal personality:
• Kitten: short, impatient mews, little grunts, and huffs.
• Puppy: soft whimpers, playful murmurs, and a tiny sneeze.
• Bunny: light squeaks, happy babbling, and giggles.

Keep the sounds natural, adorable, and comfortable to hear. Do not imitate any existing animated character’s signature voice.

Add subtle paw friction, shuffling footsteps, and cape rustling during the tussle. Lower the music slightly around important vocal reactions. Make the sneeze and comedic pause clearly audible without startling volume spikes.

CAMERA AND CONTINUITY
Use medium shots that clearly show the relationship between all three characters, with closer framing for essential facial reactions.

Maintain consistent screen direction and spatial relationships. Use clean cuts at story beats, without decorative transitions or excessive cutting.

Every action needs a readable anticipation, movement, and reaction. Keep the creatures alive through eye movement, ear movement, breathing, and small body adjustments. No stiff, motionless toy-like posing.

Exactly three characters and one central lipstick. No extra limbs, intersecting paws, duplicated props, teleporting lipstick, flickering fur, or disappearing makeup.

Generate a complete, ready-to-share 15-second video with integrated editing, original English singing, music, and synchronised sound effects, requiring as little additional post-production as possible.

No subtitles, text overlays, watermarks, or logo presentation.

Create a 30-second animated short in a polished, premium 3D animated-film style. The scene takes place in a miniature construction-themed barbershop.

**CHARACTER AND SCENE CONSISTENCY:**
A single adult male customer sits in a red barber chair throughout the entire video. He has short dark hair that has grown into one large, messy, oversized hairstyle. He wears a blue barber cape. A single barber wearing an orange construction helmet and work overalls operates miniature construction vehicles.

Keep the customer's face, clothing, body proportions, chair, barber, and hairstyle consistent in every shot. The setting, lighting, and equipment must not change. The construction vehicles are miniature tools designed specifically for trimming and styling hair.

**SEQUENCE:**

**0–5 seconds — The Setup**
Wide shot of the customer sitting nervously in the barber chair. His hair is unusually thick and tall, sticking out in every direction. The barber examines it seriously, then looks toward three miniature construction vehicles lined up beside the chair: an excavator, a crane with oversized scissors, and a tiny road roller.

**5–12 seconds — Excavation**
The miniature excavator approaches the customer's head. Its small bucket carefully removes one thin section of hair from the left side. Show the bucket lifting the cut hair away cleanly. A tiny dump truck carries the loose hair away. Repeat on the right side, creating a visibly shorter and more even silhouette. The excavator must never touch the customer's skin or face.

**12–19 seconds — Precision Cutting**
The barber operates the miniature crane. Its arm carefully positions a pair of oversized scissors above the customer's head. The scissors open and close to trim the excess hair on top, gradually creating a neat, balanced shape. Keep the customer's head still and the crane movements slow and controlled.

**19–25 seconds — The Finishing Touch**
The miniature road roller moves slowly across the top of the newly trimmed hairstyle, gently smoothing it into a clean, polished shape. It makes one complete pass and then drives away. The barber uses a small brush to remove the remaining loose strands.

**25–30 seconds — The Reveal**
The barber rotates the chair toward a standing mirror. Reveal the customer with a clean, stylish, symmetrical haircut. He smiles proudly and admires his reflection. The barber stands beside him with a satisfied expression, holding a tiny construction-site sign. End on a close-up of the customer's happy reaction.

**VISUAL AND MOTION RULES:**
- Maintain strict character, hairstyle, vehicle, and environment continuity.
- Every vehicle must remain the same size, color, and design throughout.
- Each machine performs only its assigned task.
- Show clear cause and effect: hair is trimmed only where a tool makes contact.
- Hair must disappear gradually as it is cut; never regenerate, change length randomly, or disappear between shots.
- No sudden hairstyle changes, duplicated vehicles, extra characters, floating tools, clipping, or objects passing through the customer.
- Keep the customer seated in the same chair and facing the same direction until the final reveal.
- Use smooth, physically believable movements and clear cinematic framing.

Playful visual comedy, expressive facial animation, detailed miniature machinery, warm daylight, appealing colors, and high-quality 3D animated-film rendering.

No dialogue, narration, subtitles, written text, logos, or watermarks. Sound effects only: miniature engines, hydraulic movements, scissors snipping, brushing, and a satisfying final reveal sound.

15 shots across 30 seconds, montage, every shot 2.0s: S1 0–2s, S2 2–4s, S3 4–6s, S4 6–8s, S5 8–10s, S6 10–12s, S7 12–14s, S8 14–16s, S9 16–18s, S10 18–20s, S11 20–22s, S12 22–24s, S13 24–26s, S14 26–28s, S15 28–30s. Hard cuts. Real-time, no slow motion.

Style: 8K photoreal live-action fantasy comedy, large-format film, organic grain. NOT a 3D render, NOT a game engine, NOT a game cutscene, NOT a cartoon. Pore-level skin. 24fps, 180-degree shutter, real motion blur, no warping, no morphing.

NO ON-SCREEN TEXT — CRITICAL: no captions, subtitles, titles, logos or watermarks at any point.

THE SCRIPT — CRITICAL: only these words are spoken, by the woman, nothing improvised: S7: "Ooohh... Nooo!!". S8: "Am I dreaming??". S13 and S14: a wordless scream only. Nobody else speaks.

THE TONE — CRITICAL: gentle comic fantasy. Her reactions are real, never mugging; the waiter stays dead serious and elegant.

LIVING SKY — CRITICAL: the bed floats in open sky surrounded by gathered white clouds, drifting slowly downward but never falling. Clouds drift at different speeds, vapor slides over the bed edge, wind gusts in uneven pulses lifting the duvet hem, her hair and the waiter's coat tails.

ASSETS:

@Image 1 = the woman, 100% match to reference face, hair and wardrobe.

@Image 2 = the waiter, full formal restaurant uniform: black tailcoat, white shirt, black bow tie, white gloves, slim black backpack with a pull cord on its left side.

GEOMETRY: a white-sheeted double bed centred in frame, sky and clouds on all sides, sun upper left. The waiter lands on the foot of the bed, she sits at the head. Birds travel screen-right to screen-left. S14–S15: she sits in a window seat, window on screen-left, passengers on screen-right.

FIRST FRAME: tight close-up on her sleeping face, no empty hold.

ACTION (montage, every cut on the 2-second mark):

S1 (18°/100mm close-up, gentle handheld): asleep, uneven breathing; birdsong grows loud off-frame, her brow knits, she groans and turns her head on the pillow, eyes shut.

S2 (29°/85mm, side angle): a wind gust whips her hair across her face; eyes still closed, she swats it away.

S3 (34°/65mm, high angle over the bed): she yanks the duvet up to her chin; warm sunlight crawls onto her face and she squeezes her eyes tighter, annoyed.

S4 (crash zoom): she sits bolt upright, duvet sliding off; the lens snap-zooms into an extreme close-up of her eyes flying wide open.

S5 (zoom out to 63°/30mm medium wide): reveal the bed floating in the middle of the clouds, golden sun flaring soft.

S6 (84°/22mm wide): a flock of birds enters frame-right, chirps loudly at centre frame and exits left; her head follows them, mouth open.

S7 (47°/50mm medium, handheld): she grabs her head with both hands: "Ooohh... Nooo!!"

S8 (18°/100mm close-up): utterly bewildered, head tilting, eyes darting around the clouds, lips parted, she mutters: "Am I dreaming??"

S9 (63°/30mm medium wide): a waiter drops from above in freefall and lands on the foot of the bed, mattress compressing.

S10 (47°/50mm): he lifts a polished chrome dome off a plate like a grand banquet course: just a plain sandwich. He pulls the cord on his backpack side and is yanked straight up out of frame top.

S11 (47°/50mm medium): still wrapped in the duvet, she bites the sandwich, chews, and smiles wide, savouring it.

S12 (84°/22mm wide, low behind her shoulder): a deep roar; a passenger jet bursts through the clouds, its nose filling the frame, heading straight at her.

S13 (fast horizontal orbit ending at 47°/50mm): the camera swings around her and lands on her face as she screams.

S14 (match cut, 47°/50mm, aircraft cabin): same head position, same angle, same screaming expression, now in casual travel clothes in a window seat. The scream carries over the cut; nearby passengers jolt and turn to stare.

S15 (47°/50mm): she freezes, cheeks flushing, covers her face with both hands and turns toward the window.

PHYSICS: real gravity on landings, mattress compressing and rebounding, coat tails lagging, the cord yank jolting his body upward. Only the bed floats.

ACTING: she is invested in one task: figure out where she is. Her eyes hunt the sky, the birds and the waiter, checking if this is real; in S14–S15 they dart to the staring passengers, then escape to the window. Natural blinks, never a frozen stare. The waiter keeps polite focus on her.

LIGHT & COLOUR: warm morning sun upper left, bright cloud bounce. ~70% soft white and sky blue, ~25% warm sun gold on skin, ~5% chrome glint from the dome. S14–S15: soft cool daylight through the cabin window.

AUDIO: birdsong, wind gusts, duvet rustle, mattress creak, chrome dome lift, cord snap and whoosh, jet roar, her lines, cabin hum and murmurs. No music, no score, no swell, no drone.

LOCKS: order holds — sleep, disturbed, sits up, birds, disbelief, waiter's sandwich, she savours it, jet, match cut to plane, hides face. Same face and hair throughout. No CGI look, no gimbal glide, skin never plastic.

it's a masterclass in AI *understanding* monumental scale and atmospheric depth. The IMAX 70mm vibe is palpable — from the desaturated, gritty desert palette to the almost painfully slow, deliberate camera moves that scream Villeneuve. Look closely at the lighting: it feels motivated, carving out those harsh desert textures with a level of realism that's frankly unnerving. Temporal consistency? Minimal flicker, elements hold firm. This isn't just generating video; it's generating *intent*. Workflow implications are huge: imagine pre-vis'ing entire sequences with this fidelity, then iterating on precise directorial choices in minutes. Truly groundbreaking work from @Goodmanprotocol.

My question to the industry: When AI can channel the masters so precisely, what does it mean for the *human* director's unique 'eye'? Are we becoming prompt engineers, or something more?
